newsitem.title: CHINA: China aims at aviation exports of $1.8 bln in 2000.
newsitem.headline: China aims at aviation exports of $1.8 bln in 2000.

text.p: China's aviation sector will carry out technical renovations and product upgrades in a drive to boost exports to $1.8 billion by the year 2000, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

"We are concentrating our efforts on the development of technology intensive and high value-added products," the newspaper quoted Liu Jingzhang, vice-director of Aviation Industries of China, as saying.
Aviation Industries of China had exported $3.5 billion of aircraft, machinery and electrical products during the past five years, the newspaper said without giving further details.
It also gave no figures for current export levels for the industry overall.
Beijing recently granted $5.0 billion in loans to the industry to help upgrade production of commercial airplanes and other goods, the newspaper said.
State-run Aviation Industries had found it difficult to shift production to commercial aircraft away from military planes, Liu said.
